entries.public_description: Harbormaster of Saltmere, a stout man with sun-burnt skin and a salt-stiffened beard. Keeps three ledgers on his desk and a fourth nobody is allowed to read.
entries.dm_description: Knows the lighthouse keeper left a note saying 'do not climb the spire' but has not shared this with the party.

entries.title: Daven Korr's Commission
entries.public_description: The keeper of the Saltmere lighthouse vanished six nights ago. The beacon has been dark since. Two merchant ships ran aground on the cliffs last week, their cargoes picked clean before dawn. Daven offers the party 400 silver up front and the keeper's salary for as long as it takes to put the light back on.
entries.dm_description: Daven is not paying out of pocket — the merchants' guild fronted the silver and expects results within ten days.

entries.public_description: A figure of cold blue light glimpsed at the top of the spire. Where it walks the lamps gutter and the iron rusts. It does not speak. It does not need to.
entries.dm_description: Bound to the spire by an unfinished oath. Releasing it ends the haunting but extinguishes the beacon for good.

entries.title: Wreckers' Cove
entries.public_description: Below the cliffs, a narrow shingle beach hides a sea cave the locals call Wreckers' Cove. The party found three crates of saltwater-damaged silk and a brass speaking trumpet engraved with the keeper's initials.
entries.dm_description: The trumpet is keyed to a horn at the top of the spire. Sounding either makes the other resonate.

entries.title: The Spiral Stair
entries.public_description:
The lighthouse spire has 247 iron steps and not one of them is level. Halfway up, the wall is scored with seven long parallel grooves at shoulder height. Cold air pours from above, even at midday.

Tana counted the steps twice on the way up and got a different total each time — 247 the first count, 251 the second. She blamed the wind. Bryn counted them on the way back down and got 247 twice in a row, but he insisted the landings had moved between counts. Selka refused to count and stared at the wall instead.

The grooves run for about thirty paces along the inner wall, then stop in clean iron, as if something had hit the metal and decided to leave through it instead of around it. The air on the upper side of the grooves is roughly a fingerwidth colder than the air on the lower side. You can feel the difference if you sit very still with one hand above the line and one below.

The keeper's logbook, recovered at the watchroom landing on Day Four, records two earlier incidents in the same place — once on the night of the Greenstorm in 4707, once on a still summer evening in 4711. Both entries end mid-sentence. Both have the same word scratched into the margin in a different hand than the rest of the entry: "wait".

The party did not wait. They climbed past the grooves and did not look back, and the temperature continued to drop until Selka's water-skin froze solid against her hip. By the time the watchroom door came into sight the iron of the steps was hard enough to ring like a bell when struck.
entries.dm_description:
The grooves are claw marks, but not from any beast the players will recognize. Strictly speaking, they are not claw marks at all — they are a record of motion preserved in iron, like a stonemason's mark of an animal that wasn't yet born. The Pale Lantern leaves them whenever it descends; the temperature differential is its trail.

If the party rests on the steps between the grooves and the watchroom, run the long-rest table with one column shifted toward Cold instead of Quiet. The Pale Lantern will not approach a torch held by Selka (this was Bryn's promise, not Selka's) but it will not be deterred by any other light.

entries.title: Wind direction
entries.public_description: Due west, steady. Salt smell on every gust.

entries.title: Working lamps
entries.public_description: Four of fifteen lamps in the spire still burn. The lit ones are clustered between the third landing and the fifth.

entries.title: Temperature drop
entries.public_description: About one degree per landing. Wisp's breath fogs by the fourth.

entries.title: Echoes
entries.public_description: Footsteps return slowly — about three seconds from the lower landings, longer the higher you climb.

entries.title: Pressure shifts
entries.public_description: Every eight minutes, give or take, the air pressure changes. Tana feels it in her ears first.
entries.dm_description: The shifts coincide with the Lantern moving between landings.

entries.title: Loose iron rail
entries.public_description: Between landings 14 and 15 — about a hand's-breadth section of the inner rail rattles when gripped. Two of the bolts are missing.

entries.title: Selka's torch
entries.public_description: Flickers once every other step. The pattern is too regular to be a draft.

entries.title: Wall hum
entries.public_description: When Bryn struck the wall with the pommel of his shortsword, the iron sang for a count of four before going still.

entries.title: Embedded coin
entries.public_description: Tana spotted a copper coin pressed into the iron of step 137 — half-emerged, as if the step had been poured around it.

entries.title: Wax seal fragment
entries.public_description: Wisp recovered a half-melted wax seal from the third landing's drain. The crest is unclear, but the wax is fresh — within the last month.
entries.dm_description: Matches the seal Daven uses on harbormaster correspondence.

entries.title: Bryn's hand cramp
entries.public_description: From gripping the inner rail. He has switched to the outer rail for the last five landings.

entries.title: Watchroom door
entries.public_description: Tana put her ear to it from the top step. No sound on the other side. The hinges are clean.
